overview: A narrative review, reported against SANRA, of family-led intensive care diaries and post-intensive care syndrome in adult patients and relatives, built on a documented librarian-supported search and organised in three parts: effects, harms of reading, and programme delivery and equity.
population: Studies and statements about adult intensive care patients ventilated or admitted for at least 48 hours and their relatives, published from 2005 to 2026, of any design, in English or with an available translation.
exposure: Diaries written wholly or mainly by relatives during the intensive care stay; staff-written and mixed diaries are included as comparators and reported separately.
procedures: Search of three bibliographic databases and two guideline repositories with the hospital librarian in October 2026, plus citation chasing from the included review and consensus statement. The clinical nurse specialist screens titles and abstracts; the unit's nurse educator checks a random 20 percent of exclusions and all inclusions. A fixed charting form records design, who wrote, timing and support of reading, outcomes, instruments, harms and delivery features. Synthesis is thematic, with a table of effect estimates as reported and a certainty statement for each conclusion.

outcomes.name: Post-traumatic stress symptoms in patients
outcomes.measure: As reported by included studies (proportion above a screening threshold or mean score), charted with instrument and timing
outcomes.why: The problem most often seen at the follow-up clinic and the outcome the best evidence addresses.

outcomes.name: Post-traumatic stress, anxiety and depression symptoms in relatives
outcomes.measure: As reported, with bereaved relatives charted separately
outcomes.timing: Up to 12 months after discharge or death
outcomes.why: Relatives write the diaries and carry their own post-intensive care burden.

outcomes.name: Distress and intrusive memories on reading
outcomes.measure: Any reported harm of reading, with timing and support
outcomes.why: Reading is an exposure with a known short-term cost.

outcomes.name: Offer and uptake of diaries
outcomes.measure: Proportion offered and proportion accepting, by language and family presence where reported

feasibility: Fits the 40 approved hours: about 8 for the search and screening, 16 for charting, 12 for writing and 4 for checking with the educator.
biasMitigation: Second checker for exclusions and charting
Fixed charting form agreed before screening
Family-written diaries separated from staff-written and mixed diaries

biasFlags.label: Selective citation
biasFlags.note: Limited by the documented search and the charting form.

biasFlags.label: Publication bias toward positive diary studies
biasFlags.note: Search conference abstracts and grey programme reports.

biasFlags.label: One main reviewer
biasFlags.note: Checked by the nurse educator on a random 20 percent.

flags: One balancing and one process outcome; no pooling
parsimony.simplestPath: One documented search, one charting form, three narrative sections and a table of reported estimates.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond the SANRA structure; memory reconstruction is named as the proposed mechanism, not tested.
summary: Structured narrative review with one primary outcome, one secondary, one balancing and one process outcome.
